summary: A message the user sends while an approval card waits denies the card with a reason the agent can read, then steers into the running turn (or queues on an agent that cannot steer). A deny that fails refuses the send. The backend does it on the user send path, so every client gets it.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing is stored or migrated. Open approvals live only in the registry's in-memory record and the adapters' pending maps; the deny closes them through the existing request.closed event.

automated: tests/unit/provider-registry-send-declines-approval.test.ts drives the registry with SUBMIT_USER_TURN and the legacy SEND_TURN: the open approval is denied with the reason before the message is steered (Claude, Codex) or queued (OpenCode); every open card of the chat is denied; a failed deny rejects the send and sends nothing; an open question is left alone; a managed turn (not typed by the user) does not answer a card; a turn that the durable store refuses to dispatch, or whose checkpoint fails, leaves the card open; a card stored under the root id is denied when the send names the rotated session id.
tests/unit/claude-adapter-switchboard-mcp.test.ts checks that the Claude adapter returns the deny reason as the canUseTool message, and keeps 'User denied permission' without one.
npm run typecheck and the full vitest suite.
notExercised: No live agent run: the deny-then-steer was not exercised against a real Claude, Codex or OpenCode turn, and not on a packaged build from existing user data.
Codex and ACP answers have no reason field, so those agents get a plain decline; the steered or queued message that follows is what redirects them.
The phones were not run. They send through the same backend path and update the card from request.closed, but the 'Send a message to decline and redirect' placeholder is desktop only.

Known limit, deferred: a phone outbox can deliver a message late, after a reconnect. That send then denies a card that opened after the message was written. The message carries no record of which cards the user saw, so the backend cannot tell them apart.
